translation_en: Anas reported: Aishah's merit among women is like tharid's merit over all food, tharid being bread prepared with broth. Narrated by Amr bin Awn, from Khalid bin Abdullah, from Abu Tuwalah, from Anas, from the Prophet.

Anas said the Prophet visited a young tailor in his household. The tailor served tharid. The Prophet picked out gourd, and Anas placed pieces before him; Anas loved gourd ever after. The chain is Abdullah bin Munir, who heard Abu Hatim al-Ashhal bin Hatim, from Ibn Awn, from Thumamah bin Anas, from Anas. Anas went with the Prophet to the tailor's home, where the tailor served the dish and continued working. Anas followed the Prophet's example by picking out gourd and placing it in front of him; this is why he said he loved gourd afterward.

Qatadah said Anas told them to eat. The Prophet never saw fine thin bread or a whole roasted sheep before he passed away. This report was related by Hudbah bin Khalid, from Hammad bin Yahya, from Qatadah. Qatadah said they visited Anas while his baker was standing there. Anas invited them to eat and described the Prophet's food.

Amr bin Umayyah saw the Prophet cut and eat meat from a sheep's shoulder. When called to prayer, he put down his knife, prayed, and did not renew ablution. The chain is Muhammad bin Muqatil, from Abdullah, from Maamar, from al-Zuhri, from Jafar bin Amr bin Umayyah al-Damri, from his father Amr bin Umayyah. He saw the Messenger cutting and eating the shoulder meat. When called to prayer, the Prophet placed aside the knife and meat, stood, and prayed without ablution.

Aishah said the Prophet only prohibited storing sacrificial meat beyond three days in a year of hunger, to feed the poor. They kept a sheep's foot for fifteen days. The family did not eat its fill of wheat bread with relish for three days until he died. Ibn Kathir reported the same narration. The narrators are Khalad bin Yahya, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman bin Abis, from his father, who asked Aishah. She explained the restriction was only made in a year of famine, so wealthy people would feed the poor. They used to keep a sheep's foot and eat it after fifteen days. Asked what forced them to do this, she laughed and said the family of Muhammad never ate its fill of wheat bread with a relish for three days until he died. Ibn Kathir reported the narration through Sufyan and Abd al-Rahman bin Abis.

Jabir said they took sacrificial meat as provisions to Medina during the Prophet's time. A second chain confirms this; Ata clarified they did not say they continued until reaching Medina. Abdullah bin Muhammad narrated from Sufyan, from Amr, from Ata, from Jabir. Muhammad also followed Ibn Uyaynah with this report. Ibn Jurayj said he asked Ata whether Jabir said they carried it until they reached Medina; Ata answered no.

Anas served the Prophet while traveling. He often heard him seek refuge from worry, grief, weakness, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, heavy debt, and domination by people. After Khaybar, the Prophet brought Safiyyah and held a wedding meal of dates, dried curds, and butter. He said Uhud loves us and we love it, and prayed for Medina's measures to be blessed. The chain is Qutaybah, from Ismail bin Jafar, from Amr bin Abi Amr, freedman of al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, who heard Anas. Abu Talhah took Anas riding behind him, and Anas served the Prophet whenever he stopped. Anas often heard this full supplication: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, incapacity and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by people. Anas continued serving until they returned from Khaybar with Safiyyah bint Huyayy. The Prophet had her behind him, covered with a cloak or garment. At al-Sahba he prepared hais, a dish of dates, dried curds, and butter, on a leather sheet; Anas invited men to eat. When Uhud came into view, he said it loved them and they loved it. As he looked over Medina, he prayed that Allah make the area between its mountains sacred as Ibrahim had made Mecca sacred and bless their mudd and sa measures.

Hudhayfah threw away a cup brought by a Zoroastrian, saying he had forbidden him repeatedly. He said the Prophet forbade silk, brocade, drinking from gold and silver vessels, and eating from their plates, which belong to people in this world and believers in the Hereafter. Abu Nuaim narrated from Saif bin Abi Sulayman, who heard Mujahid relate from Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Layla. They were with Hudhayfah when he asked for water and a Zoroastrian served him. Hudhayfah threw away the cup and said he had forbidden him more than once or twice. He explained that he acted this way because he had heard the Prophet forbid wearing silk and brocade, drinking from gold and silver vessels, and eating from their plates, saying these are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter.

The Prophet compared a Quran-reciting believer to a citron, pleasant in scent and taste; a believer who does not recite to a sweet date without scent; a reciting hypocrite to fragrant but bitter basil; and a non-reciting hypocrite to a scentless, bitter colocynth. The chain is Qutaybah, from Abu Awanah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Abu Musa al-Ashari. The Prophet compared four people to four foods: the believer who recites the Quran is like a citron, pleasant in fragrance and taste; the believer who does not recite is like a date, with no fragrance but a sweet taste; the hypocrite who recites is like basil, with pleasant fragrance and bitter taste; and the hypocrite who does not recite is like a colocynth, with no fragrance and a bitter taste.

The Prophet said Aishah's merit among women is like tharid's merit over all food. The transmitters were Musaddad, Khalid, and Abdullah bin Abd al-Rahman, from Anas, from the Prophet. This is another report praising Aishah's merit among women.

The Prophet said travel is a portion of hardship, keeping people from sleep and food; when a traveler completes the purpose, let him return quickly to his family. Abu Nuaim narrated from Malik, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Huraira, from the Prophet. The comparison describes the separation and discomfort of a journey; after a traveler has completed what he set out to do, he should hurry home to his family.

Al-Qasim said Barirah's case established three rulings: loyalty belongs to the one who frees a person; a freed woman may choose whether to stay with her husband; and charity received by Barirah became a gift when she gave meat to Aishah's household, so the Prophet ate it. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said Barirah's story established three precedents. Aishah wanted to buy and free her, but her owners demanded the wala, the bond of loyalty. The Prophet told Aishah she could agree to their condition if she wished, but wala belongs to the person who frees someone. After being freed, Barirah was given a choice to remain with her husband or leave him. One day the Prophet entered Aishah's home while a pot was boiling on the fire and asked for lunch. Bread and a household relish were brought. He asked if there had been meat. They said yes, but it had been given to Barirah as charity and she had gifted it to them. He said it was charity for her and a gift for them.

Aishah said the Messenger of Allah liked sweet foods and honey. Ishaq bin Ibrahim narrated from Abu Usamah, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah. She described the Prophet's love of both sweet foods and honey.

Abu Huraira said he stayed close to the Prophet to satisfy his hunger, without fine bread, silk, or servants. He pressed his stomach to gravel and asked people to recite verses he already knew so they might take him home for food. Jafar bin Abi Talib was especially generous to the poor, even sharing the last traces of food from a skin. The chain is Abd al-Rahman bin Shaybah, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhib, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Huraira. He stayed close to the Prophet when he could not eat fine bread, wear silk, or have servants. He sometimes pressed his stomach against gravel and asked someone to recite a verse he already knew so the person would take him home and feed him. He said Jafar bin Abi Talib was the best of people toward the poor: Jafar took them home and fed them what he had, sometimes bringing out an empty skin, which they cut open and licked.

Anas saw the Prophet eat gourd at a tailor's house and loved it from then on. Amr bin Ali narrated from Azhar bin Sad, from Ibn Awn, from Thumamah bin Anas, from Anas. Anas reported that the Prophet went to a tailor who served him gourd, which the Prophet ate. Anas said that he loved it after seeing the Prophet eat it.

Abu Shuaib invited the Prophet as one of five to eat food prepared by his butcher. A man followed them. The Prophet let the host choose whether to admit him, and the host welcomed him. A note says diners should share within their own table rather than pass food between tables. Muhammad bin Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from al-Amash, from Abu Wail, from Abu Masud al-Ansari. Abu Shuaib was an Ansari with a servant who was a butcher. He told the servant to prepare food and invited the Prophet as the fifth of five. A man followed them. The Prophet told Abu Shuaib that he could admit the extra man or leave him. Abu Shuaib said he would admit him. The report adds Muhammad bin Ismail's instruction that guests at one table should share with one another at that table, rather than hand food from one table to another, or else not do so.

Anas said that as a boy he accompanied the Prophet to a tailor's house. When the Prophet picked out gourd from the dish, Anas gathered it for him. The tailor returned to his work, and Anas loved gourd ever after. Abdullah bin Munir heard al-Nadr, from Ibn Awn, from Thumamah bin Abdullah bin Anas, from Anas. Anas said he was a boy walking with the Messenger. They entered the home of a young tailor who served a dish with gourd. The Prophet picked out the gourd. Anas gathered it and placed it before him while the tailor returned to his work. Anas said he continued to love gourd after seeing the Prophet do this.

Anas said a tailor served the Prophet barley bread and broth with gourd and dried meat. The Prophet picked out the gourd, which Anas loved from then on. Abdullah bin Maslamah narrated from Malik, from Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, who heard Anas. A tailor invited the Prophet to a meal, and Anas went with him. Barley bread and broth with gourd and dried meat were served. Anas saw the Prophet picking gourd from around the dish and said he had loved it ever since.

Anas saw the Prophet eat gourd from broth with dried meat, picking the pieces from the dish. Abu Nuaim narrated from Malik bin Anas, from Ishaq bin Abdullah, from Anas. Anas saw the Prophet being served broth containing gourd and dried meat, and picking the gourd from it to eat.

Aishah said the Prophet restricted storing sacrificial meat only during a year of famine so the rich could feed the poor. Their household did not eat its fill of wheat bread with relish for three days. Qabisah narrated from Sufyan, from Abd al-Rahman bin Abis, from his father, from Aishah. She explained that the restriction occurred in a year when people were hungry, so the rich would feed the poor. Her family kept a sheep's foot after fifteen days, and did not eat its fill of wheat bread with a relish for three days.

Anas said a tailor served the Prophet barley bread and broth containing gourd and dried meat. The Prophet picked gourd from around the dish; Anas began collecting it for him and loved it from that day. Ismail narrated from Malik, from Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, who heard Anas. The tailor brought barley bread and broth containing gourd and dried meat. Anas saw the Prophet pick gourd from around the dish and said he kept loving it afterward. Thumamah's version from Anas says he gathered the gourd and put it in front of the Prophet.

Abdullah bin Jafar saw the Prophet eat fresh dates with cucumber. Abd al-Aziz bin Abdullah narrated from Ibrahim bin Sad, from his father, from Abdullah bin Jafar. He said he saw the Prophet eating fresh dates together with cucumber.

Abu Uthman stayed with Abu Huraira for seven nights. Abu Huraira, his wife, and servant divided the night into three turns of prayer and waking each other. Abu Huraira also said the Prophet gave each Companion seven dates, one shriveled, and he received one.

Abu Huraira said the Prophet divided dates among them; he received five, four sound dates and one shriveled. The shriveled one proved hardest on his tooth. Muhammad bin al-Sabbah narrated from Ismail bin Zakariyya, from Asim, from Abu Uthman, from Abu Huraira. The Prophet divided dates among them. Abu Huraira received five, four dates and one shriveled date, and later found that this shriveled date was the hardest on his tooth.

Aishah said the Prophet died after they had eaten their fill of the two dark foods, dates and water. Muhammad bin Yusuf narrated from Sufyan, from Mansur bin Safiyyah, from his mother, from Aishah. She said the Prophet died after they had eaten their fill of the two dark foods: dates and water.

Jabir owed a Jewish man repayment from his date harvest, but one year his crop failed. The creditor refused to wait. The Prophet asked him to grant more time, walked through the grove, and ate a few fresh dates. He then rested in Jabir's shelter and ate another handful. After asking the creditor again and being refused, he told Jabir to harvest and repay him. Jabir gathered enough for the debt and had dates left over. The Prophet said, I testify that I am Allah's Messenger. The report explains that a trellis is a structure supporting vines or similar plants. The chain is Said bin Abi Maryam, Abu Ghassan, Abu Hazim, Ibrahim bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abi Rabiah, from Jabir. A Jewish man in Medina used to advance Jabir money against his dates, payable at harvest. Jabir had land on the road to Ruma, but one year it yielded nothing. When the creditor came to collect, Jabir had no dates to harvest and asked him to wait until the next year; he refused. The Prophet gathered his Companions and asked them to help seek more time for Jabir. They went to the palm grove. The Prophet spoke with the man, who refused. The Prophet walked among the palms, returned, and pleaded again, but the creditor still refused. Jabir brought a few fresh dates, which the Prophet ate, and showed him his shelter. The Prophet rested there, woke, and ate another handful of dates. He spoke to the creditor again, but he refused. The Prophet then went through the palms a second time and told Jabir to harvest and settle the debt. Jabir harvested enough to repay it, with some left over. He told the Prophet, who said, I testify that I am the Messenger of Allah. The report explains arish as a built shelter and says trellised plants include grapevines and similar growths.

Ibn Umar said the Prophet brought out a palm's inner core and said some trees are as blessed as a Muslim. Ibn Umar thought of the palm but stayed quiet as the youngest of ten; the Prophet then named the palm. Umar bin Hafs narrated from his father, from al-Amash, from Mujahid, from Abdullah bin Umar. The Prophet was sitting with them when the inner core of a palm tree was brought. He said some trees have a blessing like that of a Muslim. Ibn Umar thought he meant the palm and wanted to say so, but saw that he was the youngest of ten people and stayed silent. The Prophet then said that it was the palm tree.

The Prophet said whoever eats seven Ajwa dates each morning will be protected that day from poison and magic. Juma bin Abdullah narrated from Marwan, from Hashim bin Hashim, from Amir bin Sad, from his father. The Messenger said that whoever eats seven Ajwa dates each morning will not be harmed that day by poison or magic.

During a famine, Abdullah bin Umar saw people eating dates two at a time. He said the Prophet forbade pairing dates, except with a companion's permission; Shubah clarified the permission statement was Ibn Umar's own addition. Adam narrated from Shubah, from Jabalah bin Suhaym. They had a year of famine with Ibn al-Zubair and received dates. Abdullah bin Umar passed while they were eating and told them not to eat two dates together because the Prophet forbade it. He added an exception if someone asks his companion's permission; Shubah clarified that this exception was Ibn Umar's own statement.

Abdullah bin Jafar said he saw the Prophet eat fresh dates with cucumber. Ismail bin Abdullah narrated from Ibrahim bin Sad, from his father, who heard Abdullah bin Jafar say that he saw the Prophet eat fresh dates with cucumber.
